doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Ginger Baker at Louie's in Vail
summary: Lamb booked Ginger Baker at Louie's; Baker was clunky, and Lamb's Sunshine of Your Love quote during Alone Together upset him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Sit down when you listen to it. What about Ginger Baker?

Ginger Baker man, holy cow. So that was my gig in Vail that I told you about, the club called Louie’s that I had for eight, nine years. And I was bringing all these different people in and somebody had told me, I think the club owner, this young dude, he said, “Do you know that Ginger Baker moved to Denver?” I go, “You’re kidding.” And he had a horse ranch or a horse farm, or whatever. And I said, “Oh cool I’ll call him and see if I can get him.” And I called a friend who had done some work on the farm, I call up and he answers the phone. And I said, “Hey Ginger, how you doing man, this is Chuck Lamb I’m a pianist and I’d doing a gig in Vail, I’d like you to come up and play, it’s a jazz gig.” And he goes, “How much does it pay?” And he came up. That was a trip. Because — so the club is pretty small, it was sort of like Caffe Lena, probably 90 seats, smaller stage. And I show up I said you know, “Ginger I’ll meet you in the alley way to bring your stuff in.” So I go to the alley way and come around the corner, the alley way is full of drum cases that say “Cream” on ‘em. And I go in, the whole stage is filled with, you know two bass drums, toms, two floor tom toms, the whole — and he’s sitting there and he’s smoking a cigarette you know — there’s no room — I set the keyboard on the floor and it was like that. I loved it though, I loved coming around the corner and seeing those cases.

Well he was, you know, he was kind of clunky but you could tell he had played jazz and it had been a long time and he wanted to get back into it but — I’m just thinking of the one we were doing, like we were doing
So we were doing that and they were swinging and my solo
and then I started going like

Right? Started doing this thing on it, and he, it’s like he forgot where he was and he went into [scats] and the crowd went nuts and he looked at me, and you know he was pissed because that’s not what he was doing anymore but the funny part was, I mean I wasn’t doing it to bust his chops obviously, I was doing it to honor him, but you know he wanted to be known as a jazz drummer and he was really upset. But he lost it, you know, you could see him go back to it and he went right into [scats]. I always enjoyed that.
“Just when I got out you pulled me back in.” That’s funny. Wow.
